references.text: Joseph heard something that was good in his eyes - the same expression 'וַיִּיטַב בְּעֵינָיו' (it was good in his eyes) is used to express satisfaction and acceptance.
The phrase 'what is right in his eyes' refers to God's standard for what is good and acceptable.
The immediate context where Aaron explains why the sin offering was not eaten, and Moses accepts the explanation.
Moses shows humility and willingness to listen, which characterizes his throughout the Torah.
The phrase 'what is good and right in the LORD's eyes' refers to divine acceptance and approval.
The expression 'it was right in the LORD's eyes' (וַיִּישַׁר בְּעֵינֵי) is used in a similar way to express divine approval.
